name: manual_fdcff1
claim: Syncing an existing checkout to a remote branch should be a gated move, not a hard reset: refuse when the tree is dirty (untracked included) or when the move would leave a commit unreferenced, otherwise check the branch out at the exact target SHA with checkout -B. On a verified-clean tree that moves the branch and updates the files with no destructive command, and git itself refuses to overwrite anything. Return distinct refusal statuses (dirty, unpushed commits, cannot verify) so callers choose the policy; a boot-time caller should warn and leave the checkout untouched rather than die or erase.
